LESSON: LEADERSHIP IN ISRAEL: SAUL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible
Topic 2.3: Leadership in Israel: Saul
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Leadership in Israel: Saul, part of The Bible in Grade 8 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: how they exercise leadership qualities at school and in church. Why did King Saul fail in his leadership?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. discuss reasons for kingship in Israel,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Leadership in Israel: Saul in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine reasons against kingship in Israel,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Leadership in Israel: Saul in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. evaluate King Saul’s failures and the consequences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Leadership in Israel: Saul in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. deduce lessons learnt from the failures of King Saul,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Leadership in Israel: Saul in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. desire to be a God-fearing leader at school and in church.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Leadership in Israel: Saul in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. discuss reasons for kingship in Israel,

   Leadership in Israel: Saul helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. examine reasons against kingship in Israel,

   Leadership in Israel: Saul helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. evaluate King Saul’s failures and the consequences,

   Leadership in Israel: Saul helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. deduce lessons learnt from the failures of King Saul,

   Leadership in Israel: Saul helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. desire to be a God-fearing leader at school and in church.

   Leadership in Israel: Saul helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm in small groups reasons

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm in small groups reasons

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Leadership in Israel: Saul together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: Personal skills are demonstrated as learners obey God’s law.

• Digital literacy: The skill of using digital devices is portrayed as learners use the internet to research on reasons against

kingship in Israel.

Values:
• Integrity: The learners follow God’s instructions by doing the right thing even when no one is watching.

• Responsibility: The learners journal how they exercise leadership qualities at school and in church.

Link to other subjects:

• Pre-technical Studies: The learners conduct an internet search on reasons against kingship in Israel.

• English: The learners debate, brainstorm and read various Bible texts n turns.

Main points to remember:

1. discuss reasons for kingship in Israel,
2. examine reasons against kingship in Israel,
3. evaluate King Saul’s failures and the consequences,
4. deduce lessons learnt from the failures of King Saul,
5. desire to be a God-fearing leader at school and in church.

Remember the key question: how they exercise leadership qualities at school and in church. Why did King Saul fail in his leadership?
